title_en: Dalian Yutian Steel Pipe Co., Ltd. v. Dalian Free Trade Zone Hongfeng Steel Industry and Trade Co., Ltd., Haneda Steel Pipe Manufacturing Co., Ltd., and Longwangtang Subdistrict Office of Dalian High-tech Industrial Park — dispute over confirmation of property rights
ruling_gist_en: In cases concerning disputes over property right confirmation, according to the basic principles of property right changes, the request for confirmation of rights made by a party based on a transfer contract shall be treated differently for movable property and immovable property. The people's court may confirm the ownership of movable property that has been delivered. For a request by a right holder for confirmation that an immovable property registered in another person's name belongs to the right holder, the people's court shall not directly adjudicate and confirm its ownership; instead, it shall adjudicate that the other party shall handle the registration and transfer to the right holder.

full_text_en:
Dalian Yutian Steel Pipe Co., Ltd. v.
Dalian Free Trade Zone Hongfeng Steel Industry & Trade Co., Ltd.,
Yutian Steel Pipe Manufacturing Co., Ltd. (Kabushiki Kaisha),
and Dalian High-tech Industrial Park Longwangtang Subdistrict Office
— Dispute over Confirmation of Property Rights

【Ruling Summary】

In cases of disputes over confirmation of property rights, in accordance with the basic principles of changes in property rights, a request for confirmation of rights filed by a party based on a transfer contract shall be treated differently for movable property and immovable property. A people's court may confirm the ownership of movable property that has been delivered. For a request filed by a right holder to confirm that an immovable property right registered in the name of another party belongs to the right holder, the people's court should not directly render a judgment confirming the ownership, but should instead render a judgment ordering the other party to handle the registration and transfer to the right holder.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court
(2011) Min Ti Zi No. 29

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Dalian Yutian Steel Pipe Co., Ltd.
Domicile: Guanfang Village, Longwangtang, Lüshunkou District, Dalian, Liaoning Province, People's Republic of China
Legal Representative: Hiroshi Noguchi, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the company

Agent ad litem: Yang Xiaochuan, lawyer with Beijing Jiahe Law Firm

Respondent for Retrial (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Dalian Free Trade Zone Hongfeng Steel Industry & Trade Co., Ltd.
Domicile: Room 241, Block B, Taihua Mansion, Dalian Free Trade Zone, Liaoning Province, People's Republic of China
Legal Representative: Du Pifu, General Manager of the company
Agent ad litem: Huang Kaiguo, lawyer with Beijing Youbang Law Firm

Third Party at First Instance: Yutian Steel Pipe Manufacturing Co., Ltd. (Kabushiki Kaisha Haneda Pipe Manufacturing Co., Ltd.)
Domicile: 2-10-13 Minami-Kojaya, Ota-ku, Tokyo, Japan
Legal Representative: Hiroshi Noguchi, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the company
Agent ad litem: Zhao Yinwei, lawyer with Beijing Dacheng Law Firm, Shenyang Branch

Third Party at First Instance: Dalian High-tech Industrial Park Longwangtang Subdistrict Office
Domicile: Longwangtang Village, Longwangtang Subdistrict, Lüshunkou District, Dalian, Liaoning Province, People's Republic of China
Legal Representative: Zhao Baiqiang, Director of the Office
Agent ad litem: Zang Hongyu, male, Han ethnicity, born August 1, 1969, residing at 2-5-1, No. 122 Changjiang Road, Lüshunkou District, Dalian, Liaoning Province, People's Republic of China, Deputy Director of Dalian High-tech Industrial Park Longwangtang Subdistrict Office
Agent ad litem: Wang Shizhong, lawyer with Liaoning Fangshuo Law Firm

The applicant for retrial, Dalian Yutian Steel Pipe Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dalian Yutian Company), filed a request for retrial with this Court against the respondent for retrial, Dalian Free Trade Zone Hongfeng Steel Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hongfeng Company), and the third parties at first instance, Yutian Steel Pipe Manufacturing Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yutian Manufacturing), and Dalian High-tech Industrial Park Longwangtang Subdistrict Office (hereinafter referred to as Longwangtang Office), in connection with a dispute over confirmation of property rights, after refusing to accept the Civil Judgment (2010) Liao Min San Zhong Zi No. 28 rendered by the Liaoning High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Liaoning High Court). This Court rendered the Civil Ruling (2010) Min Shen Zi No. 1273 on December 8, 2010, ordering a retrial of this case. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel composed of Trial Judge Ren Xuefeng serving as Presiding Judge, and Acting Trial Judges Song Jianli and Cheng Mingzhu; later, due to work reasons, the panel was lawfully changed to Trial Judge Ren Xuefeng serving as Presiding Judge, and Acting Trial Judges Cheng Mingzhu and Ma Jinliang. The case was heard in open court on March 30, 2011, with Court Clerk Zhu Ke serving as recorder. The following persons appeared in court to participate in the proceedings: Hiroshi Noguchi, the legal representative of Dalian Yutian Company and Yutian Manufacturing; Jiang Yunguo and Yang Xiaochuan, the agents ad litem of Dalian Yutian Company; Huang Kaiguo and Zong Baozhang, the agents ad litem of Hongfeng Company; Zhao Yinwei, the agent ad litem of Yutian Manufacturing; and Zang Hongyu and Wang Shizhong, the agents ad litem of Longwangtang Office. This case is now concluded.

Dalian Yutian Company filed a lawsuit with the Dalian Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province (hereinafter referred to as Dalian Intermediate Court), alleging: On May 8, 2002, Yutian Manufacturing, in the name of Hongfeng Company, entered into a transfer contract with Longwangtang Office, and at the same time, Yutian Manufacturing and Hongfeng Company entered into another transfer contract. Pursuant to the provisions of the above two contracts, Hongfeng Company should have transferred the assets involved to the name of Dalian Yutian Company, a wholly foreign-owned enterprise established by Yutian Manufacturing. The prayers for relief were: 1. To confirm that the act of Yutian Manufacturing transferring its rights and obligations under the transfer contract concluded in the name of Hongfeng Company with Longwangtang Office to Dalian Yutian Company was valid. 2. To confirm that the ownership of the right to the use of the state-owned land of the site of the former Longwangtang Special Steel Rolling Mill under Longwangtang Office and all ground buildings, structures, and ancillary facilities including factory buildings, warehouses, substations, employee dormitories, and office buildings belonged to Dalian Yutian Company. 3. To order Hongfeng Company to assist in the transfer and registration of the above two pieces of state-owned land use rights and 13 building ownership titles to the name of Dalian Yutian Company.

The following facts were found by the Dalian Intermediate Court at first instance:

1. On the same day, May 8, 2002, at the same location, the four parties in this case respectively entered into the following three contracts: (1) Yutian Manufacturing and Hongfeng Company entered into the "Transfer Contract" (hereinafter referred to as "Transfer Contract A"). (2) Longwangtang Office and Hongfeng Company entered into the "Transfer Contract" (hereinafter referred to as "Transfer Contract B"). (3) Dalian Yutian Company, which was then a joint venture between Yutian Manufacturing and a Chinese party, and Hongfeng Company entered into the "Lease Contract".

The full text of the main body of "Transfer Contract A" is as follows: Yutian Manufacturing has decided to purchase the right to the use of the land, buildings, and ancillary facilities of the Longwangtang Special Steel Rolling Mill owned by Longwangtang Office (for details, see the transferred assets in the "Transfer Contract" entered into between Hongfeng Company and Longwangtang Office). However, since Yutian Manufacturing has not yet registered and established a wholly foreign-owned enterprise in China, it is unable to handle the relevant land and property procedures. Therefore, the transfer contract is entered into in the name of Hongfeng Company. The rights and obligations of Hongfeng Company under this transfer contract are actually assumed by Yutian Manufacturing. If Hongfeng Company suffers any economic loss due to this, Yutian Manufacturing shall compensate Hongfeng Company. Hongfeng Company undertakes that the ownership and right of disposal of the transferred assets belong to Yutian Manufacturing. When Hongfeng Company obtains the land use right certificates and building ownership certificates, it shall immediately deliver the originals to Yutian Manufacturing for keeping. If Yutian Manufacturing suffers any loss due to the fault of Hongfeng Company, Hongfeng Company shall compensate Yutian Manufacturing for the loss. If Hongfeng Company intentionally sells or mortgages the transferred property, Yutian Manufacturing may request that Hongfeng Company be held criminally liable. Hongfeng Company agrees that after Yutian Manufacturing registers and establishes a wholly foreign-owned enterprise in Dalian, China, it shall immediately unconditionally assist Yutian Manufacturing in handling the transfer procedures for the land use right certificates and building ownership certificates.

"Transfer Contract B" contains thirteen articles. The main contents relevant to the dispute are: I. Longwangtang Office agrees to transfer to Hongfeng Company the right to the use of the state-owned land of the site of the former Special Steel Rolling Mill, together with the ownership of all ground buildings, structures, underground objects, and ancillary facilities and equipment, including factory buildings, warehouses, substations, employee dormitories, and office buildings. The site covers an area of 23,453 square meters, and the total construction area of the buildings is 7,073 square meters (specific locations are shown in the attached plan of the former Special Steel Rolling Mill and list of transferred assets). II. Hongfeng Company shall pay Longwangtang Office a total transfer fee of RMB 12,000,000 (hereinafter the currency is RMB) for the above transferred assets. All costs, including land acquisition compensation fees and resettlement compensation fees, that may arise before Hongfeng Company obtains the state-owned land use right certificates and building ownership certificates, are included in the RMB 12,000,000 and shall be borne by Longwangtang Office. III. Payment of the transfer fee: 1. Hongfeng Company shall pay the transfer fee in installments, with an annual payment of RMB 1,000,000, to be paid off over twelve years. 2. Longwangtang Office guarantees that the transferred assets are free from any restrictions on disposal such as mortgages or seizures. On the condition that Longwangtang Office submits a certificate proving no such restrictions, the first installment shall be paid on May 20, 2002. Thereafter, the annual transfer fee shall be paid before May 20 of each year. IV. Transfer of property rights: Longwangtang Office shall, within three months from the date Hongfeng Company pays the first installment of the transfer fee, complete the change of registration of the building ownership certificates and land use right certificates (with a land use term of 50 years) to the name of Hongfeng Company. The relevant taxes and fees shall be borne by Longwangtang Office. After obtaining the land use right certificates and building ownership certificates, Hongfeng Company has the right to create mortgages. V. Handover of property: 1. At the same time as Hongfeng Company pays the first installment of the transfer fee, Longwangtang Office shall hand over the transferred assets (including the site and ground buildings) to Hongfeng Company. VI. Responsibilities of the parties (omitted). VII. Miscellaneous: 1, 2 (omitted). 3. Before Longwangtang Office completes the change of registration of the state-owned land use right certificates and building ownership certificates to the name of Hongfeng Company, if Hongfeng Company leases the transferred assets to other enterprises or individuals, the consent of Longwangtang Office is required. Longwangtang Office agrees that before Hongfeng Company pays the full transfer fee, Hongfeng Company may transfer the transferred assets to another enterprise, and such other enterprise shall pay the remaining transfer fee in the manner and within the time limit as agreed in this contract. Longwangtang Office agrees that Hongfeng Company may transfer its rights and obligations under this contract to another enterprise. The other rights and obligations of the parties as agreed in this contract shall continue to be enjoyed and assumed by Longwangtang Office and the assignee of the contract.

The "Lease Contract" also contains thirteen articles. The main contents relevant to the dispute are: I. Hongfeng Company agrees to lease to Dalian Yutian Company the site of the former Special Steel Rolling Mill, together with all ground buildings including factory buildings, warehouses, substations, employee dormitories, and office buildings. The site covers an area of 23,453 square meters, and the total construction area of the buildings is 7,073 square meters. II. Lease term: from the date of signing this contract until November 25, 2006. III. Rent: 1. Dalian Yutian Company shall pay an annual rent of RMB 1,000,000, excluding various expenses. 2. The first installment shall be paid on May 15, 2002, and thereafter the annual rent shall be paid before May 25 of each year. IV. Lease registration: The parties agree that Dalian Yutian Company shall be responsible for handling the relevant lease registration, and the relevant taxes and fees shall be borne by Dalian Yutian Company. V. Handover of leased assets: At the same time as Dalian Yutian Company pays the first year's rent, Hongfeng Company shall hand over the leased assets to Dalian Yutian Company.

2. On May 22, 2002, Dalian Yutian Company paid RMB 1,000,000 to Longwangtang Office in the name of repayment. Longwangtang Office also handed over the assets under Transfer Contracts A and B to Dalian Yutian Company. Dalian Yutian Company moved its place of production and business to the site of the former Special Steel Rolling Mill as agreed in the contracts involved, and has occupied and used the assets involved to date.

3. During the period of occupying and using the above assets, Dalian Yutian Company self-funded and carried out relatively large-scale renovations and expansions of the buildings.

4. Dalian Yutian Company further made the following payments: on November 26, 2003, it paid RMB 1,000,000 to Longwangtang Office in the name of repayment; on November 18, 2004, it paid RMB 200,000 to Longwangtang Office in the name of rent; on December 8, 2004, it paid two sums of RMB 500,000 and RMB 300,000 respectively to Longwangtang Office in the name of repayment; from June 29 to December 13, 2005, it paid sums of RMB 500,000 (one payment) and RMB 250,000 (two payments) to Longwangtang Office in the name of rent; on November 15, 2006, it paid RMB 1,000,000 to Longwangtang Office in the name of rent; on July 3 and December 8, 2007, it paid sums of RMB 600,000 and RMB 400,000 respectively to Longwangtang Office in the name of rent.

5. From the time when Longwangtang Office attended and witnessed the signing of the above three contracts on May 8, 2002, it was already aware that the true transferee of the above assets was Yutian Manufacturing, not Hongfeng Company. Thereafter, Longwangtang Office further clearly confirmed this through the following main acts: (1) On May 29, 2002, Dalian Yutian Company submitted to the Planning and Land Resources Bureau of Lüshunkou District a "Request for Instructions on the Renovation and Expansion Project". Its basic content was: "Our company has bought out the site and buildings of the former Special Steel Rolling Mill in Longwangtang Village, Longwangtang Town, Lüshunkou District. Pursuant to the approval in Document Da Wai Jing Mao Qi Zi [2002] No. 268 of the Dalian Municipal Bureau of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation, our company plans to carry out a renovation and expansion project on the site. Considering the current situation of the site and the production needs of Dalian Yutian Company, the following construction items need to be added ..." Longwangtang Office affixed its official seal to this document to indicate its confirmation of the content of the document and related matters. (2) On August 8, 2002, Longwangtang Office submitted to the People's Government of Lüshunkou District a "Request for Instructions on Matters Concerning the Requisition of the Land of the Former Special Steel Rolling Mill and the Change of Building Ownership Certificates". This document stated the following in explaining the reasons for the request: "From January 2001, Hiroshi Noguchi, Chairman of the Board of Directors of Yutian Manufacturing, entrusted his fully authorized representative and the then factory director of Dalian Yutian Company to negotiate with Longwangtang Office regarding the purchase of the aforementioned assets, which lasted for one year and four months. With the high attention and strong support of the District Party Committee, District Government, and relevant departments and leaders, and through the joint efforts of both Chinese and Japanese parties, the contract for Noguchi to purchase the buildings and land of the Special Steel Rolling Mill was finally formally signed on May 8, 2002. In order to fully revitalize these idle assets for many years, alleviate the financial pressure on Longwangtang Office, and also allow the buyer — Dalian Yutian Company — to commence production in the short term, with the support of the District Government leaders, we ultimately decided to sell at a price of RMB 12,000,000, to be paid in installments over twelve years, with an annual payment of RMB 1,000,000 to us." (3) On August 7, 2007, Longwangtang Office issued to Dalian Yutian Company a "Letter Agreeing that Dalian Yutian Company Continues to Perform the 'Transfer Contract'". The full text of the letter is: "Our Office entered into the 'Transfer Contract' with Hongfeng Company on May 8, 2002, stipulating that our Office would transfer to Hongfeng Company the state-owned land use right of the site of the former Special Steel Rolling Mill, together with the ownership of all ground buildings, structures, underground objects, and ancillary facilities and equipment (hereinafter referred to as the assets) at a price of RMB 12,000,000; Hongfeng Company would pay RMB 1,000,000 annually, to be paid off over twelve years. The said 'Transfer Contract' has actually been performed by Dalian Yutian Company. As of July 3, 2007, Dalian Yutian Company has paid transfer fees totaling RMB 5,600,000 (of which four installments totaling RMB 2,800,000 were collected in the name of the Industrial Office of Longwangtang Town, Lüshunkou District, Dalian). Pursuant to Article VII of the said 'Transfer Contract', our Office now agrees that Dalian Yutian Company shall acquire the assets and continue to perform the said 'Transfer Contract'."

6. On July 31, 2003, the land included in the above transferred assets was registered with the state-owned land use right in the name of Hongfeng Company as the right holder. The registration authority issued two certificates of state-owned land use right in that name for different parcels of land. On September 3, 5, and 26, 2003, the buildings included in the above transferred assets were registered with building ownership in the name of Hongfeng Company. The registration authority issued 13 building ownership certificates in that name.

7. In July 2008, the Dalian Municipal People's Government and the Dalian Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce respectively issued the "Certificate of Approval for Enterprise with Foreign Investment of the People's Republic of China" and the "Business License for Enterprise as Legal Person" confirming that Dalian Yutian Company was a wholly foreign-owned enterprise established by Yutian Manufacturing.

8. Prior to the issuance of the above certificates, on May 25, 2007, Yutian Manufacturing issued a "Confirmation Letter" to Dalian Yutian Company, which stated: "... Our company now confirms as follows: I. Dalian Yutian Company shall continue to perform the 'Transfer Contract' entered into between Hongfeng Company and Longwangtang Office, enjoy the rights and assume the corresponding obligations of the former Hongfeng Company under the said 'Transfer Contract'. II. The state-owned land use right of the site of the former Longwangtang Special Steel Rolling Mill under the said 'Transfer Contract' entered into between Hongfeng Company and Longwangtang Office, and the ownership of all ground buildings, structures, underground objects, and ancillary facilities including factory buildings, warehouses, substations, employee dormitories, and office buildings, shall belong to Dalian Yutian Company. III. Dalian Yutian Company shall be responsible for negotiating with Hongfeng Company to handle the transfer procedures for the land use right and building ownership of the assets, and shall bear all taxes and fees payable by both the buyer and the seller during the property right transfer process." On the 28th of the same month, Dalian Yutian Company held a board of directors meeting and passed a resolution agreeing to the above "Confirmation Letter".

9. After obtaining the certificate for a wholly foreign-owned enterprise, Dalian Yutian Company, based on Transfer Contract A, requested Hongfeng Company to assist in changing the registration of the transferred assets from the name of Hongfeng Company to the name of Dalian Yutian Company. This request was refused, giving rise to this lawsuit.

Dalian Intermediate People's Court found at the first instance: The focus of dispute among the parties in this case is twofold: first, to whom did Longwangtang Subdistrict Office actually transfer the state-owned land use rights and ownership of other property of the former Lüshun Longwangtang Special Steel Rolling Plant—that is, whether the actual transferee was Yutian Manufacturing Works or Hongfeng Company; second, whether the actual transferee's acquisition of rights violated Chinese law—that is, whether it should be recognized and protected by Chinese law. To clarify the rights and wrongs inherent in the two focus issues, it is first necessary to accurately analyze and position the relationship among the three contracts involved in the case—Transfer Contract A, Transfer Contract B, and Lease Contract—and then correctly determine their respective validity. From the findings of facts as described above, it can be seen that the three contracts are interrelated and cannot be formed or exist in isolation. Therefore, in determining the validity of each contract, each contract should be considered within the scope of this interrelationship. First, it should be confirmed that the Lease Contract is a sham contract, while the corresponding Transfer Contract A should be deemed genuine. The determination that the Lease Contract is a sham does not deny that the contract document itself is genuine, but rather denies that the content of the agreement expressed in the contract is genuine—that is, the content does not reflect the true intention of the parties shown in the contract, namely Hongfeng Company and Dalian Yutian Company. The grounds and reasons are twofold: First, the Lease Contract and Transfer Contract A are mutually exclusive. That is, based on the conflicting subjects and rights and obligations expressed in the two contracts, it is impossible for both contracts to be genuine; of course, it is also impossible for both to be false; one must be true and the other false. Then, which is true and which is false? On this point, not only do the interested parties—Dalian Yutian Company and Yutian Manufacturing Works—strongly assert that Transfer Contract A is genuine and the Lease Contract is false, and not only has Longwangtang Subdistrict Office, which is in a neutral position in the dispute between Dalian Yutian Company and Hongfeng Company, consistently maintained before and during the litigation that it transferred the assets in question to Yutian Manufacturing Works and that the actual transferee under the transfer contract was Yutian Manufacturing Works, but also, in a letter dated June 3, 2004, before the litigation, Hongfeng Company unequivocally admitted that the actual transferee of the assets was Yutian Manufacturing Works, not Hongfeng Company. Hongfeng Company did not provide effective and sufficient evidence to overturn this admission during the litigation; therefore, this admission is valid. Second, the most basic obligation of the transferee under a transfer contract is to pay the transfer price to the transferor. Dalian Yutian Company, in accordance with the wishes of Yutian Manufacturing Works, paid the transferor, Longwangtang Subdistrict Office, a total transfer price of RMB 6 million over six years, while Hongfeng Company paid not a single cent. Hongfeng Company claimed that because it had a Lease Contract with Dalian Yutian Company, the RMB 6 million should be deemed as indirectly paid by it to the transferor as the transfer price. This view is inconsistent with the facts and contrary to the law. Because Hongfeng Company never issued any form of receipt for rental income to Dalian Yutian Company, of course, it cannot be said that Hongfeng Company used the rent paid by Dalian Yutian Company to pay the transfer price to the transferor. Dalian Yutian Company and Hongfeng Company did not agree that the rent paid by Dalian Yutian Company to Hongfeng Company would replace Hongfeng Company's payment of the transfer price to the transferor, so it cannot be said that Hongfeng Company regarded the RMB 6 million paid by Dalian Yutian Company to Longwangtang Subdistrict Office as indirectly paying the transfer price. Second, after reaching the conclusion on the authenticity of the two contracts, it inevitably follows that the actual transferee under Transfer Contract B was Yutian Manufacturing Works. That is, according to the terms of Transfer Contract A, Yutian Manufacturing Works signed Transfer Contract B with the third party Longwangtang Subdistrict Office in the name of Hongfeng Company. The facts have fully demonstrated that all three parties voluntarily engaged in the aforementioned signing conduct.

Since the Lease Contract is a sham contract, there is no need to consider the application of law and determination of its validity. The two Transfer Contracts involve the application of law and determination of validity. Obviously, the two transfer contracts signed by the two third parties and Hongfeng Company reflect only one transfer legal relationship, not two transfer legal relationships. The combination of the two transfer contracts forms one asset transfer legal relationship, with the transferor being Longwangtang Subdistrict Office and the transferee being Yutian Manufacturing Works. Then, does the transfer by Longwangtang Subdistrict Office of the assets in question to Yutian Manufacturing Works constitute an evasion of Chinese law, as claimed by Hongfeng Company, and thus be invalid? The answer is no. Because at the time this transfer relationship was formed, the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China had already taken effect. According to that law, the hierarchy of legal norms used to assess whether the transfer relationship constitutes an evasion of Chinese law and is invalid can only be laws and administrative regulations. That is, provisions of subordinate laws below laws and administrative regulations cannot serve as a basis for determining a contract invalid. When Hongfeng Company argued in rebuttal that the asset transfer conduct between the two third parties evaded Chinese law and should be deemed invalid, it did not point out which specific mandatory or prohibitive provisions of Chinese laws or administrative regulations were violated by this transfer conduct. Upon review, no Chinese law or administrative regulation was found to prohibit or disallow the transfer and receipt of the assets in question between the two third parties. According to the basic rule and standard for judging whether conduct is legal—what is not prohibited by law may be done, and what is done is legal—it should be confirmed that, except for the transfer of ownership of underground objects as stipulated in the transfer contract, which is not legal, the transfer and receipt of the state-owned land use rights and ownership of other property in question between the two third parties are lawful and valid. The reason for not confirming the transfer of ownership of underground objects as legal is that, according to Chinese law, the ownership of underground objects belongs to the state, and this ownership is not altered by the ownership of above-ground or surface property.

Transfer Contract A has stipulated that, after Yutian Manufacturing Works establishes its wholly-owned enterprise in China, Hongfeng Company shall immediately and unconditionally assist in handling the transfer of the state-owned land use rights and building ownership. Yutian Manufacturing Works has established its wholly-owned enterprise, Dalian Yutian Company, and the contractual condition for Hongfeng Company to perform its assistance obligation has been fulfilled. Hongfeng Company should unconditionally assist in handling the transfer of the aforementioned property rights as promised. Its refusal to perform this obligation constitutes both a breach of contract and a lack of good faith.

It should be pointed out that Yutian Manufacturing Works, as a foreign enterprise and the transferee of the assets in question, and Dalian Yutian Company, at that time as a Sino-foreign joint venture invested in by Yutian Manufacturing Works and a Chinese enterprise, and as the beneficiary of the asset transfer, when contracting with Chinese enterprises and other civil subjects in China, should comply with the procedural provisions of Chinese law concerning contract formation, including the duty to truthfully disclose the true circumstances related to the contract. However, all parties on the same day and at the same place respectively participated in signing the sham Lease Contract and the transfer contracts whose names did not match their reality. Their conduct was erroneous. Although based on the reasons stated above, this error is not sufficient to render the transfer contracts invalid, this conduct has had a certain negative impact on the management of economic contracts by relevant Chinese authorities and even on the trial work of judicial organs, for which a negative assessment is given.

In summary, in accordance with Articles 8, 60, and 107 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China and Articles 15 and 33 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, this court hereby renders the following judgment: 1. The land use rights under the State-owned Land Use Certificates numbered Lüshunkou State-owned (2003) No. 0413199 and 0413204 shall belong to Dalian Yutian Company; the building ownership under the Building Ownership Certificates numbered Lüshun Village House No. 09000921, 09000922, 09000539, 09000540, 09000541, 09000542, 09000543, 09000544, 09000545, 09000546, 09000547, 09000548, 09000549 shall belong to Dalian Yutian Company; the ownership of other property, except underground objects, involved in the Transfer Contract signed between Longwangtang Subdistrict Office and Hongfeng Company on May 8, 2002, shall belong to Dalian Yutian Company. 2. Hongfeng Company shall, within 10 days after this judgment takes legal effect, assist Dalian Yutian Company in registering the aforementioned property rights certificates in the name of Dalian Yutian Company. The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 93,800 and the litigation preservation fee of RMB 5,000 shall be borne by Hongfeng Company.

Hongfeng Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Liaoning High People's Court, arguing: 1. The Lease Contract signed between Hongfeng Company and Dalian Yutian Company was the true expression of the parties' intent, complied with legal provisions, and was a valid contract. The board resolution of Dalian Yutian Company and its requests to relevant management authorities, in which it admitted to leasing the buildings and land in question from Hongfeng Company for production and operation, prove that the parties actually performed the Lease Contract, and the relationship between Dalian Yutian Company and Hongfeng Company was a lease relationship. 2. Dalian Yutian Company only provided a copy of Transfer Contract A signed between Hongfeng Company and Yutian Manufacturing Works at the first instance. According to evidentiary rules, a copy cannot be used alone as a basis for determining a case. The Dalian Intermediate People's Court's finding that Transfer Contract A was genuine and using it as a basis for the judgment violated the law. Even if the copy could be admitted, since Yutian Manufacturing Works had not registered in China at the time it signed Transfer Contract A with Hongfeng Company, it did not have the subject qualification to purchase land use rights. Moreover, without approval from relevant state authorities, it violated relevant legal provisions, so Transfer Contract A should be invalid. 3. The first-instance judgment arbitrarily changed the property rights content confirmed by the land and housing management authorities, which was an ultra vires act exceeding civil jurisdiction. 4. During the process of Dalian Yutian Company changing from a joint venture to a wholly-owned company, it submitted false materials to the industrial and commercial authorities to obtain business registration by deception, so Dalian Yutian Company lacks the subject qualification to bring this lawsuit. Therefore, it requests the revocation of the first-instance judgment and the dismissal of Dalian Yutian Company's claims.

The Liaoning High People's Court found at the second instance: The first-instance judgment made an error in identifying the parties in Transfer Contract A. In signing Transfer Contract A, party A was Hongfeng Company, i.e., the transferor; party B was Japan Tokyo Yutian Steel Pipe Manufacturing Works, i.e., the transferee. The other facts found by the first-instance judgment are confirmed.

The Liaoning High People's Court further found: On January 25, 2002, Dalian Yutian Company made the Dà Yǔ Zī Zì (2002) No. 01 "Dalian Yutian Company Twenty-Fifth Board Resolution," resolving to relocate Dalian Yutian Company and lease the original plant area of Lüshunkou District Longwangtang Special Steel Rolling Plant.

On February 10, 2002, Chen Wenqing, legal counsel of Dalian Yutian Company, provided a "Legal Opinion Letter" to the chairman of Dalian Yutian Company and Yutian Manufacturing Works, Noguchi Hiro, regarding the asset purchase matter involved in this case. Its basic content was that the ownership of the original special steel rolling mill site under Longwangtang Subdistrict Office was collective ownership, and Longwangtang Subdistrict Office had no right to transfer it externally, and it should be transferred only after being requisitioned by the government as state-owned. According to Chinese law, as a foreign legal person, Yutian Manufacturing Works could not be the transferee; the transferee must be a legal person registered in China.

On May 2, 2002, Yuan Junsheng issued a "Contact Letter (Letter of Undertaking)" to Hongfeng Company and its legal representative, Manager Du Pifu. The main content was: During the preparation process for establishing a wholly-owned enterprise, Yutian Manufacturing Works encountered difficulties in obtaining land for the new factory. First, there were legal obstacles regarding the subject qualification of Yutian Manufacturing Works to purchase land for factory construction in China; second, Yutian Manufacturing Works also faced financial difficulties. Longwangtang Subdistrict Office agreed to transfer the land and factory buildings of its special steel rolling plant. If Hongfeng Company made the purchase, it could be leased to alleviate the pressure on Hongfeng Company to pay the transfer price, thereby solving the problem of land for Yutian Manufacturing Works to build the factory. Undertakings: 1. During the production process of the wholly-owned enterprise, the procurement of raw materials, under equal conditions, would be given priority to be supplied by Hongfeng Company. 2. The products produced by the wholly-owned enterprise, under equal conditions, would be given priority to be sold by Hongfeng Company.

On May 8, 2002, Longwangtang Subdistrict Office submitted a "Certificate Letter" to Hongfeng Company, the main content of which was: Longwangtang Subdistrict Office on May 8, 2002 signed a contract with Hongfeng Company for the transfer of the factory buildings of the special steel rolling plant under Longwangtang Subdistrict Office. The factory buildings and their ancillary equipment all belonged to Hongfeng Company, and Longwangtang Subdistrict Office agreed that Hongfeng Company could lease the acquired assets to Dalian Yutian Company.

On May 13, 2002, Noguchi Hiro wrote a letter to Yuan Junsheng, the basic content of which was: Prior to this, Yuan Junsheng was an advisor to Yutian Manufacturing Works, and requested Yuan Junsheng to serve as the new general manager.

On May 15, 2002, Dalian Yutian Company submitted to the Dalian Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation Bureau the Dà Yǔ Zī Zì (2002) No. 02 "Request for Approval of the Relocation of Dalian Yutian Company's Leased Factory Premises," requesting approval for the enterprise to lease and relocate to the land and factory buildings in Guanfang Village, Longwangtang Subdistrict, Lüshunkou District, which were transferred to Hongfeng Company.

On May 23, 2002, the Dalian Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation Bureau issued Dà Wài Jīng Mào Qǐ Zì (2002) No. 268 "Reply on Approving the Change of Legal Address of Dalian Yutian Company," approving the board resolution of Dalian Yutian Company to change its legal address to Longwangtang Village, Lüshunkou District.

On May 31, 2004, Longwangtang Subdistrict Office sent a letter to Hongfeng Company, the main content of which was: Requesting Hongfeng Company to pay the 2004 asset transfer fee; otherwise, the land use certificate and building ownership certificate would be withdrawn, and the Transfer Contract signed between Longwangtang Subdistrict Office and Hongfeng Company would be voided.

On June 3, 2004, Hongfeng Company sent a letter to Dalian Yutian Company, Japan Tokyo Yutian Steel Pipe Manufacturing Works, Noguchi Hiro, and Jiang Yunguo. The "Letter" stated: "Our company received a letter from Longwangtang Subdistrict Office on June 2, 2004, requesting our company to perform the Transfer Contract signed on May 8, 2002 and pay the transfer fee within the time limit. However, on May 8, 2002, our company signed the Lease Contract with your company, and the Lease Contract, the Transfer Contract signed with your Manufacturing Works, and the Transfer Contract signed with Longwangtang Subdistrict Office are interrelated contracts—that is, the annual transfer fee of RMB 1 million payable to Longwangtang Subdistrict Office was to be paid by Dalian Yutian Company in the form of rent, and Dalian Yutian Company did not pay the amount on time within the contract period. Therefore, our company, in accordance with the notice from Longwangtang Subdistrict Office, formally declares to Dalian Yutian Company and the Manufacturing Works as follows: 1. According to the Transfer Contract signed between our company and Yutian Manufacturing Works, it is clearly stipulated that the rights and obligations of the transfer are assumed by Yutian Manufacturing Works. If our company suffers any economic losses, it shall be compensated by Yutian Manufacturing Works. 2. If any economic losses arise due to your company's or the Manufacturing Works' failure to pay the transfer fee or rent on time, our company shall not bear any responsibility, and your company and Yutian Manufacturing Works shall bear all economic losses. 3. Our company strongly requests your company and the Manufacturing Works to give our company a clear reply before June 15, 2004. If no reply is given by the deadline, in order to avoid losses, our company will have no choice but to terminate the contract with your company and the Manufacturing Works, so as to comply with the notice from Longwangtang Subdistrict Office."

On June 1, 2004, Wang Guomin issued to Yuan Junsheng a "Handover List of State-owned Land Use Certificates and Building Ownership Certificates" (hereinafter "List"), stating: "The Preparatory Group of Yutian Steel Pipe Co., Ltd. hereby returns to Lüshunkou District Longwangtang Subdistrict Office the state-owned land use certificates and building ownership certificates for the factory construction of Dalian Free Trade Zone Hongfeng Steel Industry and Trade Co., Ltd. in Guanfangzi Village, Longwangtang Subdistrict, Lüshunkou District; the specific list is as follows (omitted)." The materials mentioned that 2 state-owned land use certificates and 11 building ownership certificates were handed over. In the "Handover" column of the List, "Yuan Junsheng 15/6-2004" was signed; in the "Receiver" column, "Wang Guomin 2004.6.1" was signed; the printed date of the List was June 15, 2004.

On June 12, 2004, Yuan Junsheng issued to Du Pifu a "Receipt for State-owned Land Use Certificates and Building Ownership Certificates," stating: "Considering that your company (Hongfeng Company) has not yet paid the full transfer price under the Transfer Contract between Lüshunkou District Longwangtang Subdistrict Office and Hongfeng Company, it is suggested that the corresponding state-owned land use certificates and building ownership certificates be temporarily handed over to Lüshunkou District Longwangtang Subdistrict Office for safekeeping. Your company agrees. Now receiving 2 state-owned land use certificates and 11 building ownership certificates of Dalian Free Trade Zone Hongfeng Company." In the "Handover" column of the Receipt, "Du Pifu" was signed.

On December 27, 2004, Jiang Yunguo issued to Wang Guomin a "Handover List of State-owned Land Use Certificates and Building Ownership Certificates." In the "Handover" column of the List, "Yuan Junsheng 5/6-2004" was signed; in the "Receiver" column, "Wang Guomin 2004.6.15" was signed; the printed date of the List was June 15, 2004, and there was a handwritten note: "All documents taken away, Jiang Yunguo, 2004.12.27."

On June 30, 2008, the Lüshunkou District Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation Bureau issued the "Reply on Approving the Equity Transfer of Dalian Yutian Company," approving the change of Dalian Yutian Company from a Sino-foreign joint venture to a foreign-invested enterprise.

On September 17, 2008, Wang Guomin, then Deputy Director of Lüshunkou District Civil Affairs Bureau, appeared in court as a witness for Hongfeng Company. Wang Guomin had served as Deputy Director of Longwangtang Subdistrict Office from December 1997 to December 2004. His testimony mainly stated that Wang Guomin was in charge of investment promotion; because the Japanese side had no money to purchase the building ownership and land use rights in question, the actual purchaser was Hongfeng Company. Dalian Yutian Company and Hongfeng Company had a lease relationship, and Dalian Yutian Company directly paid the rent to Longwangtang Subdistrict Office, which helped Hongfeng Company save taxes and fees. In May 2004, when Longwangtang Subdistrict Office did not receive the RMB 1 million transfer fee, Hongfeng Company, as requested in the letter, handed over the property rights certificates for the buildings and land in question to Wang Guomin. On December 27, 2004, due to Wang Guomin's job transfer and time constraints, and being unable to contact Hongfeng Company, he handed over the property rights certificates for the buildings and land in question to Jiang Yunguo, manager of Dalian Yutian Company.

On September 17, 2008, Yuan Junsheng testified as a witness for Hongfeng Company, stating that in 2001 he was the representative of Yutian Manufacturing Plant. The main content of his testimony was that because the Dalian Municipal Government required Dalian Yutian Company to relocate, Yutian Manufacturing Plant intended to purchase the factory premises and land involved in the case. Yuan Junsheng contacted Wang Guomin, and the price was RMB 12 million. However, after various fundraising efforts, the Japanese party was unable to afford the purchase. Japanese attorney Chen Wenqing also issued a legal opinion stating that the Japanese party had no right to purchase. Since Dalian Yutian Company was a joint venture, the Chinese party did not agree to the purchase. In desperation, Yuan Junsheng negotiated with Hongfeng Company for it to make the purchase and then lease the property to Dalian Yutian Company. Accordingly, Hongfeng Company purchased the factory premises and land involved in the case, and Dalian Yutian Company leased them at an annual rent of RMB 1 million.

In its second-instance judgment, the Liaoning High People's Court held that the disputed issues in this case were: 1. Whether the true transferee of the property ownership and land use rights involved in the case was Yutian Manufacturing Plant or Hongfeng Company; 2. Whether Yutian Manufacturing Plant's acquisition of the land use rights from Longwangtang Office violated legal provisions.

Regarding the issue of whether the true transferee of the property ownership and land use rights involved in the case was Yutian Manufacturing Plant or Hongfeng Company. The first-instance court found that the true transferee was Yutian Manufacturing Plant, primarily based on the "Transfer Contract" A signed between Tokyo Yutian Steel Pipe Manufacturing Plant, Japan and Hongfeng Company, as well as a letter from Hongfeng Company. First, "Transfer Contract" A is a copy; for this important evidence that could directly prove its contractual rights, Dalian Yutian Company was unable to provide the original document and could not give a reasonable explanation for this. Second, the transferee under "Transfer Contract" A was Tokyo Yutian Steel Pipe Manufacturing Plant, Japan. Although Hongfeng Company admitted in its "Letter" dated June 3, 2004 that it had signed a transfer contract clearly naming the transferee as Tokyo Yutian Steel Pipe Manufacturing Plant, Japan, the existing evidence could not prove that Yutian Manufacturing Plant and Tokyo Yutian Steel Pipe Manufacturing Plant, Japan were the same legal person. Moreover, after the letter, on December 8, 2007, Dalian Yutian Company was still making payments to Longwangtang Office under the "Lease Contract" in the name of rent. Third, Dalian Yutian Company signed a "Lease Contract" with Hongfeng Company, and in its internal board resolutions and documents requesting relocation from relevant authorities, it acknowledged leasing Hongfeng Company's factory premises and land. The payments made by Dalian Yutian Company to Longwangtang Office were also clearly recorded as rent or repayment, not as transfer payments made on behalf of Yutian Manufacturing Plant as found by the first-instance court. Fourth, although Longwangtang Office, during the first and second instance trials and in its requests to higher authorities, considered Yutian Manufacturing Plant to be the transferee of the assets involved, it could not deny the transfer contract signed with Hongfeng Company for those assets; when the transfer payments were not received as scheduled, Longwangtang Office also sent letters to Hongfeng Company demanding payment of the outstanding amount. This indicates that Longwangtang Office recognized Hongfeng Company as the主体 obligated to repay the debt and as the transferee of the assets; Wang Guomin, the then deputy director of Longwangtang Office specifically responsible for this matter, also testified that the transferee of the assets involved was Hongfeng Company. In summary, the true transferee of the assets involved was Hongfeng Company, not Yutian Manufacturing Plant, and the first-instance court's finding on this point was erroneous. Dalian Yutian Company's claim, based on Yutian Manufacturing Plant's "Confirmation Letter," that it was entitled to the property ownership and land use rights involved lacked evidentiary support. The relevant grounds of appeal raised by Hongfeng Company were upheld.

Regarding whether Yutian Manufacturing Plant's acquisition of state-owned land use rights violated legal provisions. The subject matter of this dispute is state-owned land use rights and house ownership, and this case is a foreign-related case. Pursuant to the principle of special law precedence as stipulated in Article 8 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, which states: "Where other relevant laws have special provisions on property rights, such provisions shall apply," this case should be governed by the Land Administration Law of the People's Republic of China and the Law of the People's Republic of China on Foreign-funded Enterprises. Article 85 of the Land Administration Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "The use of land by Chinese-foreign equity joint ventures, Chinese-foreign contractual joint ventures, and foreign-funded enterprises shall be governed by this Law; where laws provide otherwise, such provisions shall apply." Accordingly, foreign-funded enterprises are subject to the Land Administration Law. However, the "foreign-funded enterprises" referred to in the Law of the People's Republic of China on Foreign-funded Enterprises do not include foreign enterprises. Under the principle of legal numerus clausus of property rights, the acquisition of property rights without legal basis is prohibited. Yutian Manufacturing Plant is a Japanese enterprise, and its acquisition of Chinese land use rights lacks legal basis.

As for Hongfeng Company's argument that during the process of Dalian Yutian Company's conversion from a joint venture to a wholly foreign-owned enterprise, it submitted false materials to the industry and commerce authorities to fraudulently obtain company registration, and thus Dalian Yutian Company lacked standing to sue. Dalian Yutian Company provided the "Reply on the Equity Transfer of Dalian Yutian Company" from the Lushunkou District Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation Bureau of Dalian, as well as the "Certificate of Approval for Foreign-invested Enterprise" issued by the Dalian Municipal People's Government and the "Business License for Enterprise Legal Person" issued by the Dalian Administration for Industry and Commerce. These documents prove that Dalian Yutian Company is a foreign-funded enterprise and has standing to sue. Whether it engaged in fraudulent registration with the industry and commerce authorities is not within the scope of the court's review.

In conclusion, the first-instance judgment contained errors in fact-finding and improper application of law. The Liaoning High People's Court, in accordance with Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (3) and Article 158 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and after discussion by its judicial committee, rendered the following judgment: 1. Reversing the first-instance judgment; 2. Dismissing all claims of Dalian Yutian Company. The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 93,800, the preservation fee of RMB 5,000, and the second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 93,800 shall all be borne by Dalian Yutian Company.

Dissatisfied with the second-instance judgment, Dalian Yutian Company applied to this Court for retrial, requesting the reversal of the second-instance judgment, the amendment to uphold the first-instance judgment, the support of its claims, and the imposition of litigation costs on Hongfeng Company. Grounds: 1. Chinese law does not prohibit foreign enterprises from acquiring Chinese land use rights and house ownership. The second-instance judgment's finding that Yutian Manufacturing Plant, as a Japanese enterprise, had no legal basis to acquire Chinese land use rights constituted an error in the application of law. (1) The State Land Administration Bureau's "Reply on the Issuance of Land Certificates for Granting and Transferring Land to Foreigners" dated March 9, 1990, stipulates that the issuance of state-owned land use rights certificates to foreign businessmen, overseas Chinese, and compatriots from Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan shall be handled by provincial-level people's governments, with the land administration departments of people's governments at or above the county level handling the specific matters in accordance with relevant state regulations. After the formal promulgation of the state regulations on the granting and transfer of state-owned land use rights, the new provisions shall apply. Article 3 of the Interim Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Granting and Transfer of State-owned Urban Land Use Rights (effective from May 19, 1990) provides that companies, enterprises, other organizations, and individuals within and outside the People's Republic of China, unless otherwise provided by law, may obtain land use rights under these Regulations to develop, utilize, and manage land. According to the above provisions, Yutian Manufacturing Plant's purchase of the assets involved complied with legal requirements. (2) The second-instance judgment found that "under the principle of legal numerus clausus of property rights, the acquisition of property rights without legal basis is prohibited." The contract involved was signed in 2002, while the Property Law of the People's Republic of China came into effect on October 1, 2007. Therefore, the Property Law should not apply to this dispute. Moreover, the principle of legal numerus clausus refers to the types and contents of property rights being legally prescribed; the Property Law does not prohibitively restrict who may acquire property rights. 2. The evidence in this case fully proves that the transferee of the assets involved was Yutian Manufacturing Plant, yet the second-instance judgment found it to be Hongfeng Company. The second-instance judgment contains multiple serious errors in the finding of basic facts. (1) The evidence in this case fully proves that the parties to "Transfer Contract" A were Yutian Manufacturing Plant, and all parties have no objection to this, yet the second-instance judgment found that "the existing evidence cannot prove that Yutian Manufacturing Plant and Tokyo Yutian Steel Pipe Manufacturing Plant, Japan are the same legal person." (2) Hongfeng Company emphasized during the trial that the copy-only "Transfer Contract" A was a letter of intent, but the second-instance judgment dismissed it on the grounds that it was a copy. The chain of evidence, including Hongfeng Company's letter and the signing video, all corroborates the authenticity of "Transfer Contract" A. The reason Dalian Yutian Company could not produce the original of "Transfer Contract" A is that it is held by Yuan Junsheng, a former employee of Yutian Manufacturing Plant, who refuses to hand it over. (3) There was no lease relationship between Dalian Yutian Company and Longwangtang Office; the payments made to Longwangtang Office were actually transfer payments. Hongfeng Company confirmed in its "Letter" that the annual transfer fee paid to Longwangtang Office was paid by Dalian Yutian Company in the form of rent. Yet the second-instance judgment erroneously found that "the payments made by Dalian Yutian Company to Longwangtang Office were clearly recorded as rent or repayment, not as transfer payments on behalf of Yutian Manufacturing Plant as found by the first-instance court." (4) The "Lease Contract" signed between Dalian Yutian Company and Hongfeng Company did not reflect the true intent of the parties, and the Lease Contract was not actually performed. Yet the second-instance judgment used this Lease Contract as one of the reasons for finding that the transferee of the assets was Hongfeng Company, which is a factual error. (5) The assets involved have always been actually possessed, used, and enjoyed for proceeds by Dalian Yutian Company, and the relevant title documents have always been kept by Yutian Manufacturing Plant and Dalian Yutian Company, fully proving that the transferee of the assets was Yutian Manufacturing Plant, and Yutian Manufacturing Plant entrusted Dalian Yutian Company to actually perform "Transfer Contract" B. (6) Longwangtang Office, as the transferor of the assets, knew from the beginning and has always recognized that Yutian Manufacturing Plant was the transferee. The second-instance judgment erroneously found that Longwangtang Office "cannot deny the Transfer Contract for the assets involved signed with Hongfeng Company." 3. The second-instance judgment also contains other serious factual errors. (1) The second-instance judgment erroneously found that "On February 10, 2002, Chen Wenqing, legal counsel for Dalian Yutian Company, issued a 'Legal Opinion' to the chairman of Dalian Yutian Company and Yutian Manufacturing Plant, Noguchi Hiroshi, regarding the purchase of the assets involved in this case." Hongfeng Company only provided a copy, not the original, and Dalian Yutian Company and Yutian Manufacturing Plant did not recognize this evidence. (2) The second-instance judgment erroneously found that "On May 2, 2002, Yuan Junsheng issued a 'Contact Letter (Undertaking)' to Hongfeng Company and its legal representative, Manager Du Pifu." This contact letter did not bear the seal of Yutian Manufacturing Plant; Yutian Manufacturing Plant clearly stated in the first instance that it never gave Yuan Junsheng such authorization, and Yuan Junsheng has a related relationship with Du Pifu. (3) The second-instance judgment erroneously found that "On May 8, 2002, Longwangtang Office submitted a 'Certificate Letter' to Hongfeng Company." This evidence does not bear the seal of Longwangtang Office, is not an original, and was not recognized by Longwangtang Office. (4) The second-instance judgment erroneously found that "On June 1, 2004, Wang Guomin issued a 'Handover List of State-owned Land Use Rights Certificates and House Ownership Certificates' to Yuan Junsheng." The date and content of this evidence prove it is not authentic. (5) The second-instance judgment erroneously found that "On June 12, 2004, Yuan Junsheng issued a 'Receipt of State-owned Land Use Certificates and House Ownership Certificates' to Du Pifu." Yuan Junsheng and Du Pifu have a related relationship, and this evidence lacks authenticity. Moreover, the second-instance judgment found that on June 1, 2004, Yuan Junsheng handed over the relevant certificates to Wang Guomin, and then found that on June 12, 2004, Yuan Junsheng received the relevant certificates from Du Pifu. This is clearly logically inconsistent. (6) The second-instance judgment erroneously found that "On December 27, 2004, due to Wang Guomin's job transfer and time constraints, unable to contact Hongfeng Company, he handed over the title documents for the factory premises and land involved to Jiang Yunguo, manager of Dalian Yutian Company." Wang Guomin's testimony is clearly illogical and lacks factual basis. (7) The second-instance judgment erroneously accepted the testimony of Yuan Junsheng, who has a close relationship with the legal representative of Hongfeng Company, as fact.

Hongfeng Company responded: 1. The second-instance judgment correctly applied the law. The "Reply on the Issuance of Land Certificates for Granting and Transferring Land to Foreigners" was abolished on January 3, 2000. The "Interim Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Granting and Transfer of State-owned Urban Land Use Rights" is merely an interim regulation. This case should be governed by Article 85 of the Land Administration Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 5 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China; the second-instance judgment correctly applied the law. 2. The second-instance judgment correctly found the facts. Dalian Yutian Company and Yutian Manufacturing Plant did not provide the original of "Transfer Contract" A, and the signing video cannot prove the existence of "Transfer Contract" A. Although Hongfeng Company recognized the authenticity of the "Letter," the letter was addressed to Dalian Yutian Company and Tokyo Yutian Steel Pipe Manufacturing Plant, Japan, not to Yutian Manufacturing Plant. If there was a transfer contract between Hongfeng Company and a Japanese enterprise, that Japanese enterprise would be Tokyo Yutian Manufacturing Plant, not Yutian Manufacturing Plant. The copy of "Transfer Contract" A is not the transfer contract mentioned in the "Letter." The copy of "Transfer Contract" A is forged. Hongfeng Company signed a "Lease Contract" with Dalian Yutian Company, and the rent paid by Dalian Yutian Company to Longwangtang Office was made because Hongfeng Company, to reduce tax burden, instructed Dalian Yutian Company to pay the rent directly to Longwangtang Office. The other alleged errors in fact found by the second-instance judgment raised by Dalian Yutian Company are all without legal basis. The second-instance judgment merely objectively described the "Legal Opinion," "Contact Letter," and other evidence without making specific findings, so there is no error in fact-finding. 3. The first-instance judgment's support of Dalian Yutian Company's claims lacked factual and legal basis. In conclusion, the second-instance judgment had clear findings of fact and correctly applied the law and should be upheld; Dalian Yutian Company's application for retrial should be dismissed.

Yutian Manufacturing Plant stated: 1. The Liaoning High People's Court erred in its finding of facts; the true transferee of the disputed property ownership and land use rights is Yutian Manufacturing Plant, not Hongfeng Company. (1) "Transfer Contract" A is authentic and valid, reflecting the true intent of the parties. (2) Yutian Manufacturing Plant and Tokyo Yutian Steel Pipe Manufacturing Plant, Japan are the same legal person; the second-instance judgment's failure to recognize this is clearly erroneous. (3) The "Lease Contract" signed between Dalian Yutian Company and Hongfeng Company did not reflect the true intent of the parties, and the receipts issued in the name of "rent" cannot prove the existence of a genuine lease relationship. 2. The second-instance judgment erred in the application of law; Chinese law clearly provides that foreign enterprises may acquire Chinese land use rights and house ownership. In conclusion, the second-instance judgment's findings of fact and application of law were clearly erroneous and should be corrected.

Longwangtang Office stated: 1. Although "Transfer Contract" A provided by Dalian Yutian Company is a copy, the signing video, the June 3, 2004 "Letter" from Hongfeng Company to Dalian Yutian Company, Yutian Manufacturing Plant, Mr. Noguchi Hiroshi, and Mr. Jiang Yunguo, and the document Lu Long Ban [2002] No. 32, in the absence of contrary evidence from Hongfeng Company, can prove the authenticity of "Transfer Contract" A. 2. The contracting parties of "Transfer Contract" A should be determined by the seals affixed, not by the translated name. 3. The acquisition of state-owned land use rights and house ownership by Yutian Manufacturing Plant and Dalian Yutian Company does not violate Chinese law.

During this Court's retrial, Dalian Yutian Company submitted to this Court one "New Evidence Catalog," one "Supplementary New Evidence Catalog," four signing photos, and one Dalian Yutian Company introduction brochure. Among them, the "New Evidence Catalog" contained four pieces of evidence: the "Explanation" from the Dalian Administration for Industry and Commerce, the "Explanation" from the Lushunkou District Economic Cooperation Bureau of Dalian, the "Business License" of Dalian Yutian Company issued by the Dalian Administration for Industry and Commerce, and the "Approval Certificate" for foreign-invested enterprises issued by the Dalian Municipal People's Government; the "Supplementary New Evidence Catalog" contained eight pieces of evidence: the "Interim Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Granting and Transfer of State-owned Urban Land Use Rights," the testimony of Director Shan Juning, the certificate of Longwangtang Office, the wire transfer and foreign exchange exchange slips for the first land transfer payment made by Yutian Manufacturing Plant on May 17, 2002, and their translations, the bank slip for the second transfer payment made by Yutian Manufacturing Plant on November 25, 2003, the notarization, authentication, and translation of Yutian Manufacturing Plant's registration, the "Technical Renovation Notification" from the Lushunkou District Economic Development Bureau of Dalian, and the approved "Construction Drawings" from the Lushunkou District Planning and Land Resources Bureau of Dalian.

Hongfeng Company argued that none of the above evidence constituted new evidence for retrial and did not recognize it. Yutian Manufacturing Plant argued that all the above evidence constituted new evidence for retrial and recognized it. Longwangtang Office argued that except for the "Interim Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Granting and Transfer of State-owned Urban Land Use Rights," which cannot be used as evidence, all other evidence constituted new evidence for retrial and was recognized.

Longwangtang Office submitted one original draft of the request report drafted by Shan Juning.

Dalian Yutian Company argued that this evidence constituted new evidence for retrial and recognized it. Hongfeng Company argued that this evidence did not constitute new evidence for retrial and did not recognize it. Yutian Manufacturing Plant argued that this evidence constituted new evidence for retrial and recognized it.

This Court, upon review, finds: The two pieces of evidence in the "New Evidence Catalog" submitted by Dalian Yutian Company, namely the "Explanation" from the Dalian Administration for Industry and Commerce and the "Explanation" from the Lushunkou District Economic Cooperation Bureau of Dalian, were formed after the second-instance judgment was rendered and constitute new evidence for retrial. These two pieces of evidence prove that the investor stated on Dalian Yutian Company's business license and approval certificate is Yutian Manufacturing Plant, but it was translated as "Japan" or "Japan Yutian Manufacturing Plant."

As for the "Testimony of Director Shan Juning" in the "Supplementary New Evidence Catalog" submitted by Dalian Yutian Company, although it was formed after the second-instance judgment, Hongfeng Company did not recognize it, and Shan Juning did not appear in court to be examined. Therefore, the probative value of this evidence will be comprehensively assessed in conjunction with other evidence. As for the "Certificate of Longwangtang Office," since Longwangtang Office participated in the first-instance, second-instance, and retrial proceedings of this case and made statements on the facts of the case, the above certificate issued by it constitutes its opinion and cannot be used as evidence to prove the facts of the case.

Except for the above four pieces of evidence, the other evidence submitted by Dalian Yutian Company and the draft request report drafted by Shan Juning submitted by Longwangtang Office objectively existed within the time limit for submitting evidence in the second instance of this case, could have been obtained and submitted by Dalian Yutian Company and Longwangtang Office, and they could not prove that their failure to submit it was not due to willful intent or gross negligence. Therefore, pursuant to Article 179, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 44 of the Supreme People's Court's "Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Procedure," and Article 10 of the Supreme People's Court's "Notice on the Application of the Provisions on Time Limits for Submitting Evidence in the 'Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Procedure,'" the above evidence does not constitute new evidence for retrial and shall not be admitted by this Court.

During the second instance of this case, Dalian Yutan Company submitted evidence of a new payment of RMB 1,000,000 in transfer fees for 2008 to the Longwangtang Office, but the second instance judgment did not admit this evidence. During the trial of this court, all parties did not dispute the fact that Dalian Yutan Company had paid a total of RMB 7,000,000 in transfer payments from 2002 to 2008 to the Longwangtang Office in the name of rent or repayment, and this court confirms this fact.

Dalian Yutan Company expressly objected to the facts otherwise found in the second instance judgment, alleging that the second instance judgment erred in fact-finding. Hongfeng Company argued that the fact-finding of the second instance judgment was correct. Upon review, this court considers that the second instance judgment found fifteen additional facts. Among them, the eighth fact, the "Letter" from the Longwangtang Office to Hongfeng Company dated May 31, 2004, the ninth fact, the "Letter Response" from Hongfeng Company dated June 3, 2004, and the thirteenth fact, the "Approval on the Equity Transfer of Dalian Yutan Company" dated June 30, 2008, had already been determined by the first instance judgment; the second instance judgment's findings were redundant. The second instance judgment also found twelve other facts, but did not analyze or determine the cross-examination status and reasons for adopting the evidence supporting these facts. Some of this evidence was copies which other parties did not acknowledge, and some was irrelevant to the facts of this case. Therefore, the first instance judgment's analysis and determination of this evidence, as well as the result of not adopting it, were correct. The second instance judgment's direct reliance on this evidence to determine the relevant facts was indeed improper and should be corrected.

During the trial of this court, Hongfeng Company applied to this court to obtain the interrogation records of the abuse of powers case conducted by the Liaoning Provincial People's Procuratorate against the relevant responsible persons of the Longwangtang Office, Ma Guiyun, Zhao Baiqiang, and Shan Juling. This court entrusted the Liaoning High People's Court to obtain the above evidence. The Liaoning High People's Court contacted the Liaoning Provincial People's Procuratorate twice, but the Procuratorate indicated that the case was still in the preliminary investigation stage and could not yet provide the above evidence, so it could not be obtained. This court considers that, under the circumstance that the above evidence cannot be obtained at present, based on the existing evidence in this case, the relevant facts can already be ascertained, so this court will no longer obtain the evidence applied for by Hongfeng Company.

Upon further trial, this court finds that: the facts found in the first instance judgment are supported by relevant evidence, and this court confirms them. The facts otherwise found in the second instance judgment lack evidentiary support, and this court does not confirm them.

Additionally, it is found that: the investor stated in the business license and approval certificate of Dalian Yutan Company is Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd., but it was translated as "Japanese Country" or "Japan Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd."

Dalian Yutan Company paid a total of RMB 7,000,000 in transfer payments from 2002 to 2008 to the Longwangtang Office in the name of rent or repayment.

This court holds that Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd. is a company registered in Japan, and this case is a dispute over the confirmation of foreign-related property rights. The immovable property and its ancillary movable property involved in the case are located within the territory of the People's Republic of China. According to Article 144 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, this case shall be tried under the laws of the People's Republic of China. The first and second instance judgments correctly applied the laws of the People's Republic of China.

Based on Dalian Yutan Company's retrial requests and reasons, Hongfeng Company's defense, and the statements of Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd. and the Longwangtang Office, there are three focal points in this case:

I. Who is the true transferee of the assets involved in the case.

1.  The legal personality of Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd. The "Transfer Contract A" clearly stipulates that the transferee of the assets involved is "Tokyo Yutan Steel Pipe Manufacturing Office, Japan", while the full name of the party, Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd., is "Yutan Steel Pipe Manufacturing Co., Ltd.". The Chinese names are inconsistent, and the second instance judgment accordingly determined that they are not the same entity. This court holds that they are the same entity for the following reasons: First, the company seal and the legal representative's personal seal affixed to "Tokyo Yutan Steel Pipe Manufacturing Office, Japan" in "Transfer Contract A" are identical to the company seal and legal representative's personal seal of Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd., a party in this case. Second, according to the facts otherwise found by this court, the sole investor of Dalian Yutan Company is Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd., but the Chinese translations of Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd. stated in the business license and approval certificate of Dalian Yutan Company all differ. Therefore, the differences in the Chinese names of Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd. arose from translation reasons. Third, during the trial of this case, no party raised any objection regarding the legal personality of Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd. in this case. Therefore, Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd., a party in this case, is the same entity as "Tokyo Yutan Steel Pipe Manufacturing Office, Japan" mentioned in "Transfer Contract A", the "Letter Response", and other evidence. The second instance judgment's determination that Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd. and "Tokyo Yutan Steel Pipe Manufacturing Office, Japan" are not the same legal person based solely on the inconsistency of the Chinese translations was indeed improper and should be corrected.

2.  Authenticity of the copy of "Transfer Contract A". Throughout the first instance, second instance, and retrial proceedings of this case, besides Hongfeng Company, the other three parties—Dalian Yutan Company, Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd., and the Longwangtang Office—consistently stated the following facts: On May 8, 2002, the four parties to this case simultaneously signed three contracts: "Transfer Contract A", "Transfer Contract B", and "Lease Contract". Now, Dalian Yutan Company has submitted a copy of "Transfer Contract A" and has explained why it cannot submit the original. Although Hongfeng Company argued that the copy of "Transfer Contract A" submitted by Dalian Yutan Company was forged, it has consistently acknowledged the authenticity of its own "Letter Response". This "Letter Response" explicitly mentions that it signed two transfer contracts with Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd. and the Longwangtang Office, and that these two transfer contracts are related to the "Lease Contract". During the trial of this case, this court explicitly required Hongfeng Company to submit the transfer contract it mentioned in the "Letter Response" which it signed with Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd., but Hongfeng Company was unable to do so. This court holds that, based on a comprehensive assessment of evidence such as Hongfeng Company's "Letter Response", the signing video recording, and the parties' statements regarding the facts of the case, it can be proven that "Transfer Contract A" genuinely existed, and that "Transfer Contract A", "Transfer Contract B", and the "Lease Contract" are related contracts. As for the specific form and content of "Transfer Contract A", because the signing parties to this contract were Hongfeng Company and Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd., both Hongfeng Company and Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd. should hold the original of "Transfer Contract A". Now, Dalian Yutan Company has submitted a copy of "Transfer Contract A" kept by Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd. and has explained why it cannot provide the original, while Hongfeng Company has consistently refused to submit the original of "Transfer Contract A" in its possession. Pursuant to Article 75 of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, this court confirms the authenticity of the copy of "Transfer Contract A" submitted by Dalian Yutan Company.

3.  Determination of the true transferee of the assets involved. In this case, "Transfer Contract A", "Transfer Contract B", and the "Lease Contract" are three interrelated contracts. Based on the terms and actual performance of these three interrelated contracts, the "Lease Contract" did not reflect the true intent of the parties and is void. "Transfer Contract A" and "Transfer Contract B" reflect the true intent of the parties, do not violate the prohibitive provisions of Chinese laws and regulations, and are legally valid.

Although "Transfer Contract B" stipulates that the transferor of the assets involved is the Longwangtang Office and the transferee is Hongfeng Company, according to the terms of "Transfer Contract A", Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd. entrusted Hongfeng Company to purchase the assets involved and to sign "Transfer Contract B". All four parties to this case were present on May 8, 2002, and witnessed the signing process of all contracts. Therefore, all parties were aware that the true transferee of the assets involved was Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd. and that an agency relationship existed between Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd. and Hongfeng Company. Article 402 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "A contract concluded by an agent in its own name with a third party within the scope of authorization of the principal, where the third party at the time of concluding the contract knows the agency relationship between the agent and the principal, directly binds the principal and the third party, unless there is conclusive evidence proving that the contract binds only the agent and the third party." Pursuant to the above legal provision, "Transfer Contract B" directly binds the Longwangtang Office and Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd. Therefore, the Longwangtang Office is the transferor of the assets involved, and Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd. is the true transferee of the assets involved.
