Hongfeng Company, by severing the connection between "Transfer Contract A" and "Transfer Contract B" and without paying any consideration, based solely on "Transfer Contract B", claims to be the transferee of the assets involved. This is inconsistent with the facts and also inconsistent with the above legal provision, and this court does not support it. The first instance judgment's determination that the true transferee of the assets involved was Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd. was correct. The second instance judgment's determination that the true transferee of the assets involved was Hongfeng Company was indeed erroneous and should be corrected.

II. Whether Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd.'s acceptance of the assets involved violates the provisions of Chinese laws and regulations.

The transferred assets stipulated in "Transfer Contract B" include the state-owned land use rights and the ownership of the above-ground buildings, structures, underground structures, and ancillary facilities and equipment. All parties to this case have no objection to Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd.'s acceptance of the ownership of the above-ground buildings and other assets. The focus of the dispute is whether Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd., as an overseas legal person, accepting the state-owned land use rights involved violates the provisions of Chinese laws and regulations. According to the provisions of the Land Administration Law of the People's Republic of China, the Urban Real Estate Administration Law of the People's Republic of China, the Interim Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Assignment and Transfer of the Right to Use State-Owned Land in Urban Areas, and other laws and regulations, China's land management adopts a system of control based on use rather than restrictions based on the user. In principle, domestic and overseas legal persons enjoy equal treatment and can legally obtain state-owned land use rights for land development and utilization. Unless otherwise specifically provided, current land management laws and regulations do not contain prohibitive or restrictive provisions regarding overseas legal persons purchasing or obtaining state-owned land use rights in China. Therefore, Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd.'s acceptance of the state-owned land use rights involved did not violate the provisions of existing Chinese laws and regulations and is legally valid. In this case, the fact that Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd. signed a contract to accept the assets involved occurred in 2002, when the Property Law of the People's Republic of China had not yet been implemented. Therefore, the second instance judgment's application of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China to determine that Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd. could not accept Chinese state-owned land use rights was indeed erroneous. Moreover, the principle of numerus clausus of real rights means that the types and content of real rights are determined by law. The second instance judgment's interpretation of this principle as meaning the acquisition of real rights is also determined by law was erroneous and should be corrected.

III. Whether Dalian Yutan Company's claims can be supported.

Dalian Yutan Company's retrial request to this court is: to revoke the second instance judgment, uphold the first instance judgment, support Dalian Yutan Company's claims, and order Hongfeng Company to bear the litigation costs. During the first instance of this case, Dalian Yutan Company raised three claims: 1. Confirm the validity of Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd.'s assignment to Dalian Yutan Company of the rights and obligations under "Transfer Contract B", which Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd. had concluded with the Longwangtang Office in the name of Hongfeng Company. 2. Confirm that the state-owned land use rights of the site of the former Longwangtang Special Steel Rolling Mill, a subordinate unit of the Longwangtang Office, and the ownership of all above-ground buildings, structures, and ancillary facilities, including workshops, warehouses, substations, employee dormitories, and office buildings, belong to Dalian Yutan Company. 3. Order Hongfeng Company to assist in transferring the registration of the above-mentioned 2 parcels of state-owned land use rights and 13 building ownerships to the name of Dalian Yutan Company.

Based on the facts already ascertained, Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd. and the Longwangtang Office issued a "Confirmation Letter" and a "Letter Regarding Consent for Dalian Yutan Company to Continue Performing the 'Transfer Contract'" to Dalian Yutan Company on May 25, 2007, and August 7, 2007, respectively, confirming that Dalian Yutan Company would continue to perform "Transfer Contract B" and enjoy the corresponding rights and obligations. Article 88 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "A party may, with the consent of the other party, assign its rights and obligations under the contract together to a third party." Therefore, with the consent of the Longwangtang Office, Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd.'s assignment of its rights and obligations under "Transfer Contract B" to Dalian Yutan Company complies with legal provisions and should be deemed valid.

Pursuant to the terms of "Transfer Contract B", Dalian Yutan Company requests confirmation of ownership of the state-owned land use rights, immovable property such as above-ground buildings, and movable property such as ancillary facilities and equipment. According to the facts already ascertained, after "Transfer Contract B" was signed, the Longwangtang Office delivered all the assets involved to Dalian Yutan Company. Article 133 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "The ownership of the subject matter transfers at the time of delivery, unless otherwise provided by law or agreed by the parties." "Transfer Contract B" does not contain an explicit agreement on the transfer of ownership of the movable property such as ancillary facilities and equipment involved. Therefore, the above legal provision should apply, and ownership of the movable property such as ancillary facilities and equipment involved transfers to Dalian Yutan Company upon delivery. The first instance judgment's confirmation of ownership of the movable property such as ancillary facilities and equipment involved was correct and should be upheld. However, for the change in real rights of immovable property, in addition to delivery, registration procedures are also required. Therefore, Dalian Yutan Company's request for confirmation that it holds the state-owned land use rights and ownership of the above-ground buildings involved lacks legal basis, and this court does not support it. The first instance judgment's direct confirmation that Dalian Yutan Company holds the real rights in the immovable property involved was somewhat improper.

According to the full content and specific wording of "Transfer Contract A", Hongfeng Company was obligated to unconditionally assist in transferring the registration of the land use certificate and building ownership certificate to the name of Dalian Yutan Company immediately after Yutan Manufacturing Co., Ltd. established its wholly-owned enterprise, Dalian Yutan Company. Now that Dalian Yutan Company has been established, its request for Hongfeng Company to assist in handling the transfer registration has a corresponding contractual basis, and Hongfeng Company should perform its obligation in accordance with the contract. Therefore, the first instance judgment's support for Dalian Yutan Company's third claim, regarding Hongfeng Company handling the transfer procedures, was correct. The second instance judgment's dismissal of all of Dalian Yutan Company's claims was indeed erroneous and should be corrected.

In summary, some of Dalian Yutan Company's retrial requests have relevant factual and legal basis and should be supported. The second instance judgment had unclear fact-finding and erroneous application of law, which should be corrected. Although the first instance judgment had clear fact-finding, the application of law and the result of the judgment were also somewhat improper and should be corrected. This case, after deliberation by the Judicial Committee of this court, pursuant to the provisions of Article 153, Paragraph 1, Items (1) and (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, is adjudged as follows:

1.  Revoke the Civil Judgment (2010) Liaomin San Zhong Zi No. 28 of the Liaoning High People's Court and the Civil Judgment (2008) Damin Er Chu Zi No. 63 of the Dalian Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province;

2.  Confirm that the ownership of the ancillary facilities and equipment under the transfer contract concluded by Yutan Steel Pipe Manufacturing Co., Ltd. in the name of Dalian Free Trade Zone Hongfeng Steel Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. with the Longwangtang Subdistrict Office of Lüshunkou District, Dalian City belongs to Dalian Yutan Steel Pipe Co., Ltd.;

3.  Dalian Free Trade Zone Hongfeng Steel Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. shall, within seven days from the date this judgment takes effect, transfer the registration of the land use rights under the "People's Republic of China State-Owned Land Use Certificates" numbered Lüshunkou Guoyong (2003) Zi No. 0413199 and 0413204 and the building ownerships under the "Building Ownership Certificates" numbered Lüshuncun Fang Zi No. 09000921, 09000922, 09000539, 09000540, 09000541, 09000542, 09000543, 09000544, 09000545, 09000546, 09000547, 09000548, 09000549 to the name of Dalian Yutan Steel Pipe Co., Ltd.

4.  Dismiss the other claims of Dalian Yutan Steel Pipe Co., Ltd.

The first and second instance case acceptance fees are RMB 93,800 each, and the litigation preservation fee is RMB 5,000, totaling RMB 192,600, to be borne by Dalian Free Trade Zone Hongfeng Steel Industry & Trade Co., Ltd.
